bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Moves Towards Safer Motherhood - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Moves Towards Safer Motherhood 07 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar has recorded significant improvement in maternal and newborn healthcare , with institutional deliveries, antenatal care and postnatal services showing substantial growth, according to NFHS-6 data cited in a recent report. Key Points: Institutional Deliveries: Institutional deliveries in Bihar increased from 76.2% to 81.1% , indicating greater access to healthcare facilities during childbirth. Early Antenatal Care: First-trimester antenatal care (ANC) increased from 52.9% to 63.9% , reflecting improved early pregnancy monitoring. ANC Coverage: Women receiving at least one ANC service increased from 81.6% to 94% , indicating wider engagement with formal healthcare services during pregnancy. Postnatal Care: Mothers receiving postnatal care within two days of delivery increased from 57.3% to 69.9% . Newborn Care: Newborns receiving care within the first two days after birth increased from 59.3% to 76.2% . Role of Government Hospitals: Government hospitals accounted for 57.5% of deliveries in Bihar, with their share rising to 58.4% in rural areas . Safer Motherhood: The simultaneous improvement in ANC, institutional deliveries and postnatal care indicates greater use of formal healthcare services throughout the pregnancy–delivery–postnatal cycle . Significance: Improved maternal and newborn healthcare can contribute to reducing preventable complications during pregnancy and childbirth. bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi writes to PM Modi, seeks declaration Bihar flood as 'national disaster' - 10net
bihar_raw_news.content: National Tejashwi writes to PM Modi, seeks declaration Bihar flood as 'national disaster’ September 7, 2026 7:26 PM IST 2 min read 47 views Live Patna, Sep 7: Leader of the opposition in the Bihar Assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, on Monday wrote a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi demanding declaration of the state's floods as a “national disaster” and immediate financial assistance of Rs 5,000 crore to the state to tackle the situation. In his letter, Yadav alleged that the “financially bankrupt” Bihar government “persistently failed in taking response, mitigation and adaptation measures” and was “indifferent” to helping flood victims. Fed by heavy rainfall, rivers have swelled and inundated 13 districts of Bihar, affecting 27 lakh people, officials said. So far in September, the state received 69.1 mm of rain, which is 55 per cent above normal. Describing flood relief and rescue arrangements made by the NDA government in the state as “grossly inadequate,” Yadav claimed that the Bihar ministers and the ruling alliance’s Union ministers and MPs elected from Bihar appeared “helpless, ineffective and incapable” in the wake of the disaster. “They have neither been able to get the Centre to declare the severe floods a national disaster nor have they been able to strongly demand a special relief and assistance package for Bihar,” he said. The RJD leader alleged that the state's contingency fund and other financial resources were “used for routine government expenditure,” creating an acute shortage of funds for relief during the ongoing disaster. “I urge the Central government to provide immediate financial assistance of Rs 5,000 crore to Bihar and announce a special flood relief package,” Yadav wrote in his letter. In the letter, he demanded that the Union government order an independent review or CAG audit of the state's financial and disaster-management preparedness, as well as the transactions of the state's Contingency Fund. Yadav also demanded immediate provision of additional rescue boats, food, drinking water, medicines, cattle fodder, temporary shelters, and special financial assistance to vulnerable groups in worst-hit areas. He sought the assistance of the Army and Air Force helicopters, wherever required, for flood relief and rescue operations. “A long-term flood resilience mission should be launched, covering river and embankment management, drainage, revival of water reservoirs, modern flood forecasting, an effective water-management policy and suitable agreements with neighbouring countries,” the RJD leader said. He urged the central government not to “discriminate against Bihar” in any manner and to provide special central assistance to the state as part of a humanitarian and national responsibility. bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India Today Insight Why Bihar govt is advising citizens not to fish in Nepal floodwaters Mood of the Nation Offer:Use promo code MOTN2026 to get ₹500 off on all Print + Digital subscriptions SUBSCRIBE Why Bihar govt is advising citizens not to fish in Nepal floodwaters Unknown, unusually big fish have arrived in parts of Bihar with the floodwaters, followed by reports of people falling ill after consuming them Advertisement Amitabh Srivastava UPDATED: Sep 7, 2026 18:57 IST Edited By: Ashish Mukherjee In July 2004, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav, then Union railway minister, stood before a roomful of mediapersons with a gamcha in hand and offered an unusual way of looking at Bihar's floods. The rising waters, he said, were not entirely a calamity: the floods gave poor people a chance to eat the fish that normally lived in ponds owned by the rich—rare, delicious fish they could not dream of eating in the dry season. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story It was classic Lalu remark: a joke, a piece of class politics and a way of turning a disaster into an argument about who owned Bihar's resources. Twenty-two years later, Bihar's BJP-led government has issued the opposite instruction: do not eat fish the flood has brought. On August 31, the department of dairy, fisheries and animal resources issued an advisory, warning people against eating, buying or selling unknown and unusual fish that had arrived in parts of Bihar with the floodwaters from Nepal. The warning followed reports of people falling ill after eating some of these fish. The government also asked people to report unusual catches to the district fisheries officer or local administration. The contrast with Lalu's 2004 fish story is almost too perfect. Then, the floods were a temporary leveller: water breached the boundaries of private ponds and fish that belonged to somebody else suddenly became available to everybody with a net. In 2026, the state is asking people to resist precisely that instinct—to see unfamiliar fish in floodwaters as not a windfall but a potential health hazard. The reason is prosaic. Floodwater carries almost anything with it. Fish can be swept out of ponds, rivers, lakes and reservoirs and carried far beyond their habitat. In the process, they may pass through drains, come into contact with dead animals and decaying matter, and be exposed to other pollutants. The Bihar advisory warns that such exposure can increase the risk of bacterial, viral and fungal contamination and pose health risks. This is important since fish is food, commerce and livelihood. The advisory is blunt. People are being told not to consume unfamiliar or unusually appearing fish. They have been asked not to buy or sell such fish caught from floodwaters, and not assume that an unfamiliar fish is edible merely because it resembles a species they normally eat. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Agriculture Department to provide subsidy on sugarcane machinery to 3,173 farmers
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Muzaffarpur: The Agriculture Department has decided to provide financial assistance to sugarcane farmers for purchasing agricultural machinery used in sugarcane cultivation. Under the scheme, permits will be issued to 3,173 farmers in sugarcane-producing districts to purchase machinery with a subsidy of 40% to 50%, Hindustan reported. The subsidy will cover 44 types of agricultural machinery. The department has also issued guidelines regarding farmers’ eligibility and the conditions for availing the subsidy. Selected farmers will have to purchase the approved sugarcane machinery within 30 days of the permit being issued. The subsidy amount will be transferred directly to the farmers’ bank accounts after they purchase the machinery and complete the prescribed online process, including submission of purchase receipts and other required documents. According to the Joint Director of Agriculture, Tirhut Division, all four districts of the division, including Muzaffarpur, have been covered under the scheme. A total of 117 farmers from the four districts will be eligible to benefit from the scheme.

bihar_raw_news.title: 27 lakh people in 13 Bihar districts hit by floods; CM inspects community kitchens
bihar_raw_news.content: 27 lakh people in 13 Bihar districts hit by floods; CM inspects community kitchens Bihar floods affect 27 lakh people in 13 districts. CM Samrat Choudhary directs relief, rescue operations. Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, other rivers flow above danger levels. By PTI September 7, 2026, 3:14:18 PM IST (Published) 2 Min Read (Photo Credit : Representative AI image ) Around 27 lakh people have been affected as rivers overflowing in Bihar inundated 13 districts, prompting Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to direct officials on Monday (September 7) to ensure prompt relief and rescue operations while inspecting community kitchens for flood victims in Vaishali and Bhagalpur. Officials said 190 community kitchens were being run in various flood-hit districts, while 1,429 boats have been pressed into service for relief and rescue operations. CM Samrat Choudhary and his deputy Vijay Kumar Choudhary inspected the community kitchens in Vaishali and Bhagalpur, and directed the local authorities to continuously monitor river embankments and keep a close watch on vulnerable areas. Authorities have already sounded an alert in downstream areas of the Ganga after the river touched its highest flood mark at Gandhi Ghat and Hathidah in Patna. Fed by heavy rainfall, rivers have swelled and inundated 13 districts of Bihar, affecting 27 lakh people, officials said. So far in September, the state received 69.1 mm of rain, which is 55% above the normal. Engineers have been asked to keep resources and machinery ready, while people in flood-prone areas have been advised to avoid going near rivers, they said. At Gandhi Ghat in Patna, the Ganga was flowing at 50.41 metres at 6 am on Monday, which is 1.57 metres above the danger level. The Gandak river has been flowing above the danger level at Dumariaghat and Hajipur, the Kosi at Baltara and Kursela, the Budhi Gandak at Khagaria, the Ganga at Hathidah, Bhagalpur, Kahalgaon, Buxar and Munger, the Punpun at Sripalpur, the Bagmati at Benibad and the Ghaghra at Darauli, the officials said. bihar_raw_news.title: AI to Create Super Teachers in Bihar , Cricket Bowling to Explain Maths - Jagran Josh
bihar_raw_news.content: AI to Create Super Teachers in Bihar, Cricket Bowling to Explain Maths By Faham Ehraj Last Updated: Sep 7, 2026, 14:18 IST Bihar government teachers will now get AI training with Google. Master trainers will teach AI to all teachers for smarter and easier classrooms. Read the article to know more details. AI to Create Super Teachers in Bihar Register for Result Updates Bihar government teachers will now receive AI training with the help of Google India. Resource persons from Google India will provide AI training to selected teachers in every district of Bihar, These trained teachers will then act as master trainers. They will make all other teachers proficient in this technology. This training has been running in Maharashtra since last July. Under the National Education Policy 2020 every teacher must complete 50 hours of professional development training every year. Keeping this in mind teachers are being given AI training. Scroll to get more details. AI Makes Learning Simple and Fun Students often see mathematics as a difficult subject. AI changes this completely. When a teacher uses AI to teach mathematics the tool creates an everyday story related to the lesson. Suppose a teacher wants to teach fractions. The AI tool uses the popular cricket example. A bowler comes to bowl and an over has six balls. After the first ball the AI asks to explain the fraction ⅙ of the ball is bowled. After the second ball it asks to explain 2/6 of the ball is bowled. The 2/6 is reduced to ⅓. So for the second ball it says the bowler has completed ⅓ of the over. During a live TV match if the screen shows 8.3 overs the AI explains that the bowler has completed eight and a half overs. AI can also bring poems to life. An english teacher was teaching Robert Frost’s poem Fire and Ice. The students were not interested and their attention was distracted. The teacher used an AI image generator and asked it to create a picture where half the world is burning and the other half is covered in snow. The picture was created in a few seconds. Seeing this live picture the children started visualizing the poem. They began to enjoy understanding its meaning. AI Will Save Hours of Teachers Work Teachers spend hours preparing lesson plans by hand or on a computer. With AI prompts a lesson plan is ready in just a few minutes. Teachers also need to prepare question papers for exams. This takes hours of brainstorming with AI. They can prepare question papers and test worksheets instantly. They can also prepare new content for teaching in the class. Many times children do not understand the language of books. AI helps explain a lesson in easy simple language. AI also creates a desire to study in weak students. This means the style of education in Bihar is going to change. bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court to Hear Plea on Airfare and Airline Charges Today | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 SC to hear on September 7 plea seeking guidelines to control unpredictable fluctuations in airfare Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on Monday a plea seeking regulatory guidelines to control the “unpredictable fluctuations” in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines in India. As per the apex court’s cause list of September 7, the matter would be heard by a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta. On August 17, the Centre had told the top court that it has fast-tracked the framing of rules under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, which is aimed at modernising India’s aviation sector, and the same would be finalised within three weeks. The government had placed the draft rules before the bench in a sealed cover and said some final discussions were going on. The apex court had noted that Additional Solicitor General Anil Kaushik, appearing for the Centre, sought three-week time to get the draft rules finalised and place it before the court. The top court is hearing a plea filed by social activist S Laxminarayanan, who has sought a robust and independent regulator that ensures transparency and passenger protection across the civil aviation sector and regulatory guidelines to control the “unpredictable fluctuations” in airfare and ancillary charges imposed by private airlines in India. Senior advocate Ravindra Srivastava, appearing for the petitioner, had argued before the bench that till the time the new rules come into force, the old rules are operating. Questioning the “lack of willingness” on the part of authorities and the effectiveness of the existing mechanism, he had argued that airlines were charging exorbitant fares. On July 13, the top court had asked the Centre to place the rules framed under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, before it. It had said the rules be placed before it in a sealed cover, irrespective of whether those have been placed before Parliament. While hearing the plea on May 15, the apex court said there should be some rationalisation of airfares and asked the Centre to provide relief to flyers. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who was then appearing in the matter for the Centre, had told the bench that the new enactment of 2024 had come into effect in January 2025 and the corresponding rules were in the process of being prepared. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

The registry is a multicentre national database for secure and de-identified collection of real-world data on patient outcomes in heart valve interventions. India Valve Registry The India Valve Registry is designed to record clinical data from hospitals across India that perform valve interventions. It collects de-identified patient information, which is a standard method used in medical databases to protect personal identity while retaining clinical utility. Advanced heart valve interventions have been performed in India since 2011, but no continuous national database existed before this launch. Join Our WhatsApp Channel Tanushree Singh Updated Sep 7, 2026 9:49 AM IST RVNL last week emerged as the lowest bidder (L1) for another railway infrastructure project from East Coast Railway worth Rs 404.88 crore, including GST. Shares of Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd ( RVNL ) gained as much as 2 per cent in Friday's trade after the railway PSU received a Letter of Award worth Rs 903 crore, including GST, from SJVN Thermal Private Ltd for a project in Bihar. The RVNL stock opened at Rs 216.20 over its previous close of Rs 212 on the BSE. It touched a high of Rs 216.50, representing a gain of 2.12 per cent. Advertisement Read More RVNL said it received the Letter of Award from SJVN Thermal Private Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Ltd, for the construction of a permanent siding along with an aerial connection via track from the plant boundary to Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur in Buxar, Bihar. The project is part of the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project. According to the company's exchange filing, the project has an order value of Rs 903.01 crore, including GST, and is scheduled to be executed over 36 months. The contract falls within RVNL's normal course of business. The scope involves construction of a permanent siding and an aerial track connection linking the plant boundary with Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur for the Buxar Thermal Power Project. Advertisement The order comes after RVNL last week emerged as the lowest bidder (L1) for another railway infrastructure project from East Coast Railway worth Rs 404.88 crore, including GST. That project has an execution period of 30 months. The East Coast Railway project involves execution of roadbed, minor and major bridges, road under bridges/limited-height subways, building works, ballast supply and permanent-way linking. The scope also includes utility shifting, signalling and telecommunication works, electrification, power-supply arrangements and modification of high-tension and low-tension lines. The said work is connected with the development of a third railway line between Nergundi-Barang and Khurda Road-Vizianagaram on the 385-km Bhadrak-Vizianagaram section. bihar_raw_news.title: India's TB Fight: How Indigenous Innovation Can Drive Tuberculosis Elimination
bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 Gearing up to eliminate tuberculosis Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Gobardhan Das | Simarjot Kaur For much of the developed world, Tuberculosis (TB) is a disease of the past. For India, it remains one of the country’s biggest public health and economic challenges. Nearly one in every four TB patients worldwide are from India, making the disease not just a healthcare concern, but a test of the nation’s scientific capability, policy execution and innovation ecosystem. As India is marching towards becoming a developed nation by 2047, eliminating TB is no longer simply about saving lives, it is about reducing healthcare costs and demonstrating India’s ability to solve a global problem through indigenous innovation. Over the past decade, India has significantly strengthened its fight against Tuberculosis (TB) through the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). Although the ambitious 2025 elimination target remains a work in progress, it has accelerated investments in diagnostics, treatment and patient support. The results are encouraging. According to the WHO Global TB Report 2025, India’s TB incidence has declined by 21%, from 237 to 187 cases per lakh population between 2015 and 2024, almost twice the global rate of decline. During the same period, TB mortality fell by 25%, while treatment coverage improved dramatically from 53% to 92%, reflecting stronger case detection and better access to care. Digital platforms such as Ni-kshay, nutritional support through the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana, expanded molecular diagnostics and nationwide community campaigns under TB Mukt Bharat have together transformed India’s TB response, laying a strong foundation for eventual elimination. Despite this progress, the battle is far from over. Drug-resistant TB remains a serious threat, requiring longer treatment, higher costs and more complex clinical management. Delayed diagnosis, undernutrition, diabetes, overcrowded living conditions and social stigma continue to fuel transmission. Addressing these issues will require stronger public health systems alongside continued scientific innovation. Scientific innovation is changing the landscape of TB treatment. New medicines such as Bedaquiline, Delamanid and Pretomanid have significantly improved outcomes for patients with drug-resistant TB by enabling shorter and more effective treatment regimens. Researchers are also working on improved vaccines, rapid diagnostics and host-directed therapies that strengthen the body’s immune response against infection. India is not merely adopting these innovations; it is actively developing them. The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and its National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis (NIRT) are leading research on new diagnostics, treatment strategies and disease surveillance. The Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) are supporting startups and research institutions working on vaccines, diagnostics and novel therapeutics, helping build a stronger indigenous innovation ecosystem. Indian industry is also playing a crucial role. Companies such as Macleods Pharmaceuticals, Lupin, Cipla and Cadila Pharmaceuticals manufacture affordable anti-TB medicines that are used across India and also exported to many low and middle-income countries. Meanwhile, Molbio Diagnostics has developed the portable Truenat platform, enabling rapid molecular diagnosis even in remote healthcare settings. bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 CM Shivakumar calls for deeper Indo-US ties in tech, innovation Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Sunday called for deeper India-US cooperation in technology, education, innovation, research, investment and culture, pitching Bengaluru as a key technology and innovation hub in the strategic partnership between the two countries. Addressing an event marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, in the presence of US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor, Shivakumar said the India-US relationship was moving beyond traditional government-to-government engagement, with universities, scientists, entrepreneurs, startups and businesses playing an increasingly important role. “Washington and New Delhi may guide the strategic partnership between our countries. But Bengaluru and Silicon Valley give it a powerful technological dimension,” he said. Shivakumar said Karnataka was keen to expand cooperation with the US in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, digital technologies and scientific research. “Karnataka’s ambition is to be among those who shape, build and lead the technologies of tomorrow,” he said. Highlighting economic ties, the chief minister said more than 1,000 American companies operated in Karnataka, accounting for nearly half of the total American corporate presence in India, while more than 80,000 American citizens lived in Bengaluru. “The strongest connection between our two countries will be built not only through commerce, but through knowledge, ideas and innovation,” Shivakumar said. The CM said Karnataka was building an ecosystem for next-generation technologies and investments, including KWIN City and a semiconductor park, besides plans for an AI tech park with an AI hub and India’s first public sector AI university. Shivakumar also highlighted the state’s growing presence in advanced manufacturing, aerospace and defence, saying Foxconn, which manufactures Apple iPhones, had its largest presence in India in Bengaluru. He said the state’s Aerospace Park was also expanding. Referring to Bengaluru’s emergence as a global technology and education hub, Shivakumar said the city had strengthened its role in India’s international engagement. “(Infosys founder) Narayana Murthy played an important role in shaping Bengaluru’s global journey, including his association with BIAL,” he said. Recalling former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s observation that while people once travelled to Delhi and Mumbai, “today, the world comes to Bengaluru”, Shivakumar said the city had become a major global gateway to India. “The world looks at India through Bengaluru,” he said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM inspects flood relief operations in Vaishali, Saran; distributes cheques to kin of victims
bihar_raw_news.content: Home News National News Bihar CM inspects flood relief operations in Vaishali, Saran; distributes cheques to kin of victims In Short Bihar CM inspects flood relief operations in Vaishali, Saran; distributes cheques to kin of victims IANS Created On: 7 Sept 2026 5:58 PM IST Comment Share : X Amid the ongoing floods in Bihar, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Patna: Amid the ongoing floods in Bihar, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary visited Vaishali and Saran districts to assess the ground-level situation and review relief and rescue operations. The Chief Minister began his visit in Hajipur, where he conducted a surprise inspection of a flood relief camp near the old toll plaza. He reviewed arrangements for flood-affected families, including the community kitchen and other essential facilities, and interacted directly with people staying at the camp. During the inspection, Choudhary checked the quality of food being prepared at the community kitchen and enquired about the facilities available to the affected families. He also visited the Anganwadi centre operating at the relief camp and interacted with the children there. The Chief Minister also distributed ex-gratia compensation cheques of Rs 4 lakh each to the next of kin of around half a dozen people who had died due to drowning during the floods. Essential relief materials were also distributed among affected families. Choudhary directed officials to ensure that there were no lapses in relief and rescue operations and that all essential facilities reached flood victims without delay. Speaking to the media after inspecting the camp, the Chief Minister said that some inconvenience was inevitable during a natural disaster but asserted that the situation was currently under control. He said the water level of the Ganga was continuously receding, with a decline of around 17–18 cms recorded. He added that officials and administrative teams were working diligently on the ground to provide relief and carry out rescue operations. Choudhary expressed hope that flood-affected people would receive considerable relief within the next two to three days, following which normal life would gradually return. He also stressed the need for continued vigilance in vulnerable areas and instructed the administration to ensure that relief supplies reached every affected family. Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Chaudhary accompanied the Chief Minister during the inspection. Several local MLAs from Vaishali, along with the District Magistrate, Superintendent of Police and other senior administrative officials, were also present. The local administration had made extensive arrangements for the Chief Minister’s visit, with security personnel deployed at the relief camp and surrounding areas while officials supervised both security and relief arrangements. bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Floods 2026: Ganga Breaks Records, Districts Impacted and IMD Warnings By Manisha Waldia Last Updated: Sep 7, 2026, 15:30 IST Bihar Floods 2026: Ganga breaches all-time record levels at Gandhi Ghat in Patna, over 22.4 lakh people affected across 12 districts. Check impacted areas, IMD rain alerts, NDRF rescue and other updates Bihar Floods 2026: Ganga Breaks Records, Districts Impacted and IMD Warnings Due to heavy rainfall in parts of northern India as well as their neighboring states, the flood situation in Bihar has worsened. In Patna, the Ganga River has exceeded the highest level of flood water ever recorded leading to the inundation of wide low-lying areas, diara areas, and vital large utility infrastructure. More than 22.4 lakh people in more than 12 districts have been affected by floods. Emergency alerts have been issued and rescue teams deployed by the Bihar Disaster Management Department and the district administrations leading to the establishment of relief camps. Below is the elaborated account of the water level records, flooded areas, railway services affected, IMD predictions, and the relief operations carried by the government. Bihar Floods 2026:Ganga River Water Levels Go Beyond 2016 Max Record According to the Water Resources Department (WRD), there has been significant rise of water level along the main course of Ganga Gandhi Ghat (Patna): Ganga at 50.57 meters has set an all-time high, breaking erstwhile record of 50.52 meters set on August 21, 2016. The water level of river Ganga will mean that water is more that 2 meters higher than the danger mark declared by the authorities. Pandarak (District Patna): The river level ahs reached 43.92 meters thus breaking the earlier record of 43.73 meters set in August 2021. Downstream Alert at Hathidah: As there is vast water influx from above, alerts have been issued for gauging stations in Hathidah, Munger, Kahalgaon and Bhagalpur. List of Impacted Districts and Population Affected According to official updates, approximately 22.42 lakh people across 12 key districts are experiencing severe inundation: District Situation Patna Ganga above highest flood level Bhagalpur Floodwaters affecting villages and low-lying areas Munger River levels above danger mark Vaishali Flood alerts and rescue operations Bhojpur Waterlogging and inundation Buxar Rising Ganga levels Begusarai High flood alert Nalanda Vulnerable due to rising river levels Khagaria Impact from Kosi and Ganga systems Katihar Riverine flooding concerns Gopalganj Gandak above danger mark Saran Flood preparedness measures activated Flood-affected Region: Villages, farmland, and the urban fringes at places like Patna, Fatuha, Raghopur, and Bhagalpur are submerged in water, prompting people to seek refuge in safe places. Other Flooding Rivers: The Gandak (near Dumariaghat and Hajipur), Kosi (near Baltara and Kursela), Burhi Gandak (at Khagaria), Punpun (at Sripalpur), and Bagmati rivers (at Benibad) are also flowing above their danger marks. bihar_raw_news.title: RVNL: From Railway Project Agency to Diversified Infrastructure Leader | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 07, 2026 RVNL: BUILDING CONNECTIONS, CREATING POSSIBILITIES Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service From a railway project implementation agency to a diversified infrastructure enterprise India’s progress is reflected in the infrastructure that connects people, regions and opportunity. In little more than two decades, Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL), created to accelerate railway development, has evolved into a diversified infrastructure enterprise spanning railways, metros, bridges, tunnels, digital infrastructure, power, renewable energy and rolling stock. EMERGING FROM A NATIONAL VISION RVNL emerged from the National Rail Vikas Yojana announced by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on 15 August 2002 to strengthen railway infrastructure and accelerate capacity creation. Incorporated on 24 January 2003 under the Ministry of Railways, it received its Certificate of Commencement of Business on 18 February 2003 and began operations with its Board in 2005. Its journey has included Category-I Mini Ratna status in 2013, listing on the BSE and NSE in 2019, and Navratna status in 2023. FROM RAIL INFRA TO ALL INFRA RVNL’s transformation is increasingly defined by its move “from Rail Infra to All Infra.” Building on strengths in engineering, project management, systems integration, tunnelling, bridges and electrification, it has expanded into metros, roads and highways, ports, power and transmission, telecommunications, renewable energy and rolling-stock manufacturing. In FY2025-26, its order book stood at approximately Rs 99,262 crore, reflecting its wider infrastructure footprint. ENGINEERING LANDMARKS The New Pamban Bridge in Tamil Nadu represents RVNL’s bridge-engineering capability, combining rail connectivity with a navigational opening for marine traffic. The 125-km Rishikesh-Karnaprayag Rail Link is another major undertaking, involving extensive tunnelling through challenging Himalayan terrain. RVNL has also contributed to metro projects including Indore’s Yellow Line and Kolkata’s Majerhat Metro Station, built over an existing railway yard and drainage canal. Its project portfolio includes the 8.86-km Vallarpadam-Idappally rail link in Kerala. DIGITAL CONNECTIVITY AND SUSTAINABLE INFRASTRUCTURE RVNL’s participation in BharatNet’s Middle-Mile Network extends its role into rural digital connectivity. Sustainability is also becoming integral to execution through renewable energy, energy-efficient designs, recycled materials, responsible resource use and measures aimed at strengthening asset resilience. HYDRO-IRRIGATION: A NEW FRONTIER RVNL is expanding into hydropower and irrigation by leveraging its capabilities in large civil works, tunnelling and water conveyance. Its assignments include the Rammam-III Hydroelectric Project for NTPC in the Teesta Basin, involving major civil and hydro-mechanical works. In Rajasthan, RVNL is executing the Upper High-Level Canal component of the Mahi Bajaj Sagar Project through an RVNL-SCC Infrastructure joint venture. The project includes a canal and piped distribution network designed to provide irrigation to approximately 41,903 hectares. AN EMERGING GLOBAL INFRASTRUCTURE PLAYER RVNL’s ambitions increasingly extend beyond India. Its international activities span the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa, taking Indian engineering and project-execution capability to growing infrastructure markets. STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS AND TECHNOLOGY Special Purpose Vehicles, Joint Ventures and Public-Private Partnerships have supported RVNL’s expansion by combining capital, expertise and execution capability. According to a press release issued by the Ministry, the dialogue, involving Mayors and Local representatives from 63 NCR cities, marks the first instance of such a large-scale engagement organised by the Ministry with elected representatives of local bodies on the issue of air pollution. Yadav emphasised that a scientific and data-based approach to air pollution control must reach the grassroots, with public representatives playing a central role in translating action plans into effective implementation on the ground. He encouraged Mayors and local representatives to lead by example and mobilise citizens to prevent avoidable pollution and ensure cleaner, healthier urban environments. He added that Urban Local Bodies are the first responders and can bring phenomenal change with guided actions and hence have a very important part to play in this issue. He called upon public representatives to familiarise themselves with the powers and responsibilities of local bodies in air pollution control and solid waste management and to take the first positive steps to create replicable examples for citizens. Yadav urged local bodies to increase green cover by planting local and drought-resistant grass species along roads to help contain dust pollution. He also called for greater avenues for public participation in ensuring effective cleaning, preventing plastic use and biomass burning, and checking pollution from non-conforming industries and vehicles. national_raw_news.title: Indian firm linked to Estonia ammunition deal has no dealings with Defence Ministry
national_raw_news.content: Indian firm linked to Estonia ammunition deal has no dealings with Defence Ministry Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Indian firm linked to Estonia ammunition deal has no dealings with Defence Ministry ANI | Updated: Sep 07, 2026 15:07 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 7 (ANI): The Indian company allegedly linked to a deal to supply artillery shells to Estonia for onward delivery to Ukraine has no dealings with the Ministry of Defence or the Indian armed forces, Defence officials said. The clarification comes after the company was linked to an alleged ammunition procurement controversy in Estonia, which has led to the resignation of now former Estonian Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur. Against this backdrop, officials clarified that the company has not received any supply orders from the Indian armed forces. However, they added that it may have supplied equipment to state police forces, as claimed on its website. "NECO Defence has no dealings or supply orders from our armed forces, but they may have supplied to state police as claimed on their website," Defence officials told ANI. The officials also said the company has no connection or dealings with the Ministry of Defence (MoD). "No connection or dealings with MoD," the officials added. NECO Defence is part of a Nagpur-based group of companies involved in the steel manufacturing business. They added that the company recently acquired Datasel, a small Italian firm involved in the manufacture of small arms and ammunition. The firm also has a manufacturing facility in Romania, which has a contract to fill artillery shells for supply to Estonia and their onward delivery to Ukraine, the officials further said. Hanno Pevkur announced on September 2 that he would step down following controversy over an alleged arms deal to supply Ukraine. The controversy centred on the use of European Union funds to allegedly purchase artillery shells from companies that had no previous track record of producing such weapons. Earlier, Euronews, citing Estonian public broadcaster ERR, reported that the Estonian government had struck a deal in 2024 to acquire artillery shells for Ukraine, paying 70 million euros upfront from the EU's European Peace Facility to fund the purchase. national_raw_news.title: DAC clears capital acquisition proposals worth about Rs 1.10 lakh crore for the defence forces - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Defence DAC clears capital acquisition proposals worth about Rs 1.10 lakh crore for the defence forces Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), under the chairmanship of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on September 07, 2026 accorded Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) i.e., in-principle administrative approval to various acquisition proposals of the Defence Forces at an estimated cost of about Rs 1,10,000 crore. For the Indian Army, approval was granted for the procurement of Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Recce Vehicles, High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Mechanical Mine Layers (MML), Advanced Light Helicopters (ALHs), Trawl Tanks and Sarvatra Bridge System. The CBRN Recce Vehicles will be capable of detecting, identifying, monitoring and marking of areas contaminated with CBRN agents. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The MMLs will achieve the desired operational capability in terms of fast and responsive minelaying in difficult terrains. The ALHs will execute complex missions across all terrains and operational situations for the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. The Trawl Tanks and Bridge System will be utilised to provide composite crossings to fighting formations during operations in varied terrains. For the Indian Navy, AoN was accorded for the procurement of Arudhra Radars, Design & Development and subsequent procurement of Marine Gas Turbines (MGT). Arudhra Radar will replace the existing Air Route Surveillance Radars at various Naval Air Stations and MGT, a warship propulsion system, will reduce dependency on foreign vendors. For the Indian Air Force, approval was granted to various proposals to enhance the war-fighting capability of fighters, transports and helicopters. Approval was also accorded for procuring Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer (GBMPJ) and installing Defence Forces Secure Access Card (DEFSAC) System. The GBMPJ will provide effective jamming against radars of adversaries and DEFSAC will replace existing paper based Identity Card/Passes/Permits with an interoperable Radio Frequency Identification-based smart cards system. national_raw_news.title: Ayurveda Day 2026 to become National Health Communication campaign: MoS Prataprao Jadhav
national_raw_news.content: Ayurveda Day 2026 to become National Health Communication campaign: MoS Prataprao Jadhav Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Ayurveda Day 2026 to become National Health Communication campaign: MoS Prataprao Jadhav ANI | Updated: Sep 07, 2026 18:29 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 7 (ANI): Union Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, Prataprao Jadhav, on Monday said that Ayurveda Day 2026 should go beyond being a government programme and evolve into a people’s movement and a national health communication campaign. Addressing the Curtain Raiser Press Conference for the 11th Ayurveda Day at the National Media Centre, New Delhi, Jadhav highlighted that the world is increasingly looking towards preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles, nutrition, wellness and holistic health, areas where India has a rich tradition and experience, a press release from the Chief Minister’s office said. He emphasised that Ayurveda Day is not merely an occasion to celebrate India’s heritage but an opportunity to connect this heritage with the health requirements of the future. In line with the vision of Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Jadhav highlighted the need for a healthcare approach where health goes beyond treatment of disease and encompasses healthy habits, appropriate diet and daily routines, mental balance and harmony with nature, the press release said. The release added that Jadhav outlined three important areas that will guide this year’s Ayurveda Day campaign: “Integrative Healthcare for Better Health Outcomes", with a focus on leveraging the expertise and strengths of different systems of medicine for better health outcomes; “Evidence, Research and Innovation in Ayurveda", emphasising research, evidence and innovation as essential pillars for the wider global acceptance and future development of Ayurveda; and “Ayurveda for Community Wellbeing and Sustainable Living", highlighting the role of Ayurveda in promoting the wellbeing of individuals, families and communities while encouraging sustainable living. Jadhav emphasised the important role of the media in disseminating accurate, evidence-based and simple information on Ayurveda to the public. He noted that while Ayurveda enjoys widespread acceptance, it is important to address misconceptions and ensure that citizens have access to reliable information. He called upon the media to support the campaign and take the message of Ayurveda to homes, schools and colleges, young people including Gen Z, and rural and urban communities, the press release said. Calling for a stronger connection between India’s traditional knowledge and contemporary healthcare needs, Jadhav said that the campaign should seek to connect tradition with knowledge, knowledge with evidence, evidence with innovation, and innovation with public welfare. Sanjeev Sharma, Vice-Chancellor, National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), Jaipur, highlighted the key features of Ayurveda Day 2026, which will focus on evidence-based Ayurveda, research and innovation, integrated healthcare, community wellbeing, and sustainable living. He also outlined the major programmes planned for the occasion, including the National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Awards 2026, along with key initiatives such as new programmes at NIA Jaipur, safety dossiers on medicinal plants, Standard Treatment Guidelines for skin diseases, a report on the Ayush Services Sector,...

national_raw_news.title: PM to Visit Gujarat and Maharashtra on 8th September - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister's Office PM to Visit Gujarat and Maharashtra on 8th September PM to Lay Foundation Stones, Inaugurate and Dedicate to the Nation Development Projects Worth More Than ₹35,000 Crore in Vadodara PM to Dedicate Three Key Sections of Western Dedicated Freight Corridor to the Nation, Marking Completion of the Project PM to Lay Foundation Stone for three Railway Projects and three Highway Projects PM to Inaugurate Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai Theme of GFF 2026: “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum - Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance” Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 11:51AM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Gujarat and Maharashtra on 8th September 2026. At around 12 noon, Prime Minister will lay the foundation stones, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth more than ₹35,000 crore in Vadodara. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. At around 5:45 PM, Prime Minister will inaugurate Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai and address the gathering as well. PM in Vadodara Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation three important sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC), covering 326 route kilometres and developed at a cost of more than ₹20,700 crore. These include the New Sanand (N)- New Makarpura, New Umbergaon-New Saphale and New Saphale- New JNPT sections. The direct connectivity of Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) will facilitate faster movement of EXIM cargo, strengthen connectivity between industrial centres and ports, reduce logistics costs and help decongest Mumbai’s railway network. With the commissioning of these sections, the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) network will stand fully operational across its entire length. The dedicated freight infrastructure will further strengthen the country’s logistics ecosystem by improving multimodal connectivity, reducing transit time and facilitating seamless movement of cargo across different regions. Prime Minister will also flag off freight train services from New Sanand (North), New Makarpura, New Umbergaon and New JNPT, Mumbai. In addition, he will flag off a new passenger train service between Tanda Road and Vadodara (Pratapnagar). Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the Jobat–Tanda Road new rail line, developed as part of the Chhota Udepur–Dhar project. The new rail line will connect remote and tribal areas of Alirajpur with the national rail network. Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for three railway projects spanning 329 kilometres and costing more than ₹9,700 crore. These include the Vadodara-Ratlam third and fourth lines, Miyagam Karjan-Choranda–Malsar gauge conversion and the Vishwamitri-Dabhoi doubling project. The projects will enhance passenger and freight capacity, ease congestion and strengthen connectivity between Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone for three National Highway projects costing around ₹1,780 crore. These include six-laning of the Kamrej-Chalthan section of NH-48; construction of additional structures, including major bridges over the Tapi and Narmada, on the Vadodara-Surat section of NH-48; and grade-separated structures at Abhava, Mindhola and Khajod junctions on NH-53. national_raw_news.title: Government Strengthens Transparent and Timely Delivery of Post-Matric Scholarships for ... - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Transparent and Timely Delivery of Post-Matric Scholarships for Scheduled Caste Students Online Application Systems, Direct Benefit Transfer and Aadhaar-Seeded Payments Support Efficient Scholarship Delivery Regular Monitoring and Outreach Strengthen Access to Scholarship Benefits across the Country Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 2:55PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste students through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The Scheme supports eligible students in pursuing post-matriculation and post-secondary education and promotes greater access to educational opportunities. Applications under the Scheme are invited through designated State scholarship portals or the National Scholarship Portal. As the implementing agencies, States and Union Territories determine the principal arrangements for inviting applications, scrutiny, verification and other implementation processes, with suitable mechanisms established at their level. The release of the Central share is linked to the disbursement of the corresponding State or Union Territory share and the submission of finally verified beneficiary data on the National Scholarship Portal. This coordinated process is designed to support accurate verification and accountable transfer of scholarship assistance. The Direct Benefit Transfer under the Scheme was introduced in 2021-22. The system has enabled a simpler and faster flow of funds while strengthening accurate beneficiary targeting, de-duplication, efficiency and transparency. Aadhaar-seeded bank payments have further streamlined the payment process and helped reduce delays in scholarship disbursement. To expand awareness of the Scheme, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment undertakes outreach through advertisements in national and regional newspapers, social media campaigns and regular follow-up with States and Union Territories. These efforts are intended to help eligible students and their families access timely information about application and implementation processes. Implementation is reviewed regularly through national-level Chintan Shivirs, regional meetings and national conferences involving stakeholders and officials of States and Union Territories. These consultations provide a platform to review operational issues, strengthen coordination and improve delivery of scholarship benefits. The Ministry also reviews and revises its schemes in consultation with concerned stakeholders and in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The continuing focus is on accessible application systems, reliable payments, effective implementation and transparent delivery of benefits to eligible Scheduled Caste students across the country. **** PR-103- TAR/KV/GA/RK (Release ID: 2307396) Visitor Counter : 254 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Kannada Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Strengthens Transparent and Timely Delivery of Post-Matric Scholarships for Scheduled Caste Students Online Application Systems, Direct Benefit Transfer and Aadhaar-Seeded Payments Support Efficient Scholarship Delivery Regular Monitoring and Outreach Strengthen Access to Scholarship Benefits across the Country Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 2:55PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste students through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.
